title: Sp4 perturbation induces a Tsga10/Abhd11 module in thalamic and midbrain glutamatergic neurons
exact_observed_result: Sp4 assignment produced FDR-supported responses almost exclusively in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, with shared Tsga10 and Abhd11 induction and partial support from Svip, Strada, Dnajc4, and Tuba1a.
biological_interpretation: SP4 dosage perturbation exposes a caudal glutamatergic transcriptional state distinct from the developing-cerebellar SP4-NMDAR axis.

evidence_records.statistics: 183 perturbed cells versus 23679 matched controls; 14 genes at FDR<0.05. Top effects included Stxbp2 logFC=-1.069, score=-7.400, FDR=2.35e-09; Svip logFC=0.643, score=6.267, FDR=3.17e-06; Tspan17 logFC=-0.695, score=-6.182, FDR=3.64e-06; Strada logFC=0.469, score=5.842, FDR=2.23e-05; Tsga10 logFC=0.772, FDR=7.23e-04.
evidence_records.description: The thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic class contained the strongest FDR-corrected Sp4 perturbation signature.

evidence_records.statistics: 158 perturbed cells versus 20353 matched controls; 4 genes at FDR<0.05. Tsga10 logFC=1.092, score=5.790, FDR=1.22e-04; Abhd11 logFC=0.725, score=5.355, FDR=7.45e-04; Tuba1a logFC=0.368, score=4.901, FDR=0.00554; Rassf4 logFC=-1.402, score=-4.621, FDR=0.0167.
evidence_records.description: Midbrain glutamatergic neurons showed the second FDR-corrected Sp4 signature.

evidence_records.statistics: The remaining 20 Sp4-profiled classes each had zero genes at FDR<0.05 with 28-91 perturbed cells and 3465-15039 matched controls. Their smallest per-class FDR values were 0.1068 in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 0.1212 in 217 P MY Pineal Glut, and 0.1756 in 052 Pvalb Gaba.
evidence_records.description: Most Sp4-assigned cell classes did not produce a multiple-testing-corrected transcriptomic response.

caveats: Sp4 mRNA rose rather than fell in the strongest signature, so the result should not be scaled as a measured transcript knockdown.

prior_expectation.summary: Prior literature and pathway context were taken from the resolved report references; the observed Perturb-seq signal either refines expected gene function by cell type or marks an exploratory response-state neighbor where noted in caveats.

citations.citation: UniProtKB entries Q02446 and Q62445, Transcription factor Sp4.
citations.supports: Curated annotation that SP4 is a nuclear Sp1-family C2H2 zinc-finger transcription factor that binds GT/GC boxes and is a probable transcriptional activator.

citations.citation: Human Protein Atlas entry ENSG00000105866, SP4.
citations.supports: Reports SP4 as a transcription factor with low regional specificity and detection across human and mouse brain regions.
